hero.description: Synapse turns your conversations into a knowledge graph. People, places, goals, emotions, patterns. All structured, all connected. An AI that learns who you are, not just what you said last.

pullQuote: "I needed a space that remembers my patterns, not just my words. Synapse doesn't start over every time. It notices when I'm spiraling the same way I did last month — and helps me catch it earlier."

comparison.title: Context changes everything
comparison.description: Same conversation. One AI has context, the other doesn't. The difference is obvious.

regular.text: I had a terrible day. Everything feels overwhelming again.
I'm sorry to hear that. Have you tried taking some deep breaths or going for a walk? Sometimes a change of scenery helps.
I told you last week this keeps happening after meetings with my boss...
I don't have context from previous conversations. Can you tell me more about what's going on with your boss?

synapse.text: I had a terrible day. Everything feels overwhelming again.
I hear you. The last three times you've described this 'everything crashing' feeling, it followed tense interactions with David. Did something happen in today's meeting?
Yes. He dismissed my proposal in front of everyone. Again.

That pattern of public dismissal has been a consistent trigger for you — it connects to the authority dynamics we've explored before. Last time, the body scan helped you move from shutdown back to your window. Want to try that now, or do you need to just be angry first?

pipeline.title: Memory engineering, not memorization
pipeline.description: Four steps from conversation to structured knowledge.

steps.title: Converse
steps.desc: Talk about your day, your goals, your worries. Every session gets captured automatically.

steps.title: Ingest
steps.desc: Sessions are processed through Graphiti, extracting entities and relationships into Neo4j.

steps.title: Compile
steps.desc: Your knowledge graph is compiled and injected into future sessions as structured context.

steps.title: Evolve
steps.desc: Each conversation refines the graph. The more you talk, the better it gets.

personas.title: Different needs, one memory
personas.description: Every companion reads the same knowledge graph but brings a different lens. Therapeutic depth, gentle reflection, or practical momentum.

list.name: Compass
list.desc: Maps your emotional patterns across conversations. Connects today's anxiety to recurring triggers using your history. Grounded in ACT, DBT, and Polyvagal Theory — it builds psychological flexibility, not just coping skills.

detail.subtitle: Therapeutic companion — neuroaffirmative by default

theories.name: Acceptance & Commitment Therapy (ACT)
theories.desc: Builds psychological flexibility through values clarification, cognitive defusion, and willingness to sit with difficult emotions instead of avoiding them.

theories.name: Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT)
theories.desc: Teaches distress tolerance, emotion regulation, interpersonal effectiveness, and mindfulness — skills for navigating intensity without shutting down.

theories.name: Polyvagal Theory
theories.desc: Reads your nervous system states — safe/social, fight/flight, or shutdown — and helps you move between them without pathologizing any response.

theories.name: Somatic Experiencing
theories.desc: Brings awareness to where emotions live in your body. "Where do you notice that?" is not a cliché — it's a doorway to regulation.

useCases: Processing recurring anxiety, grief, or anger with someone who remembers the full pattern
Tracking your window of tolerance and nervous system states over time
Building internal authority and self-validation instead of depending on external advice
Exploring difficult relationships and dynamics without being told to "see the other side"
Complementing formal therapy with a memory-powered companion between sessions
detail.approach: Compass never minimizes, never defaults to toxic positivity, and never suggests empathizing with someone who hurt you unless you choose to. It prioritizes your subjective reality, asks one meaningful question at a time, and mirrors your energy — steady in crisis, curious in exploration.

list.name: Solace
list.desc: A gentle, unhurried space for emotional reflection. Notices shifts in your mood and energy over time. Draws on Positive Psychology, self-compassion research, and mindfulness — without ever making it feel like homework.

detail.subtitle: Wellbeing companion — reflective, not prescriptive

theories.name: PERMA Model (Seligman)
theories.desc: Explores five pillars of flourishing: Positive emotions, Engagement, Relationships, Meaning, and Accomplishment — a map for what makes life feel full.

theories.name: Self-Compassion (Kristin Neff)
theories.desc: Practices three components: common humanity (you're not alone in this), mindfulness (noticing without drowning), and self-kindness (treating yourself as you'd treat a friend).

theories.name: Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR)
theories.desc: Present-moment awareness, non-judgment, and beginner's mind — turning attention into a skill rather than a chore.

useCases: Daily emotional check-ins without the pressure of "doing therapy"
Tracking what brings you joy, flow, or calm — and being reminded when you forget
Processing ambivalence, numbness, or the feeling of "not knowing" without judgment
Building emotional literacy: naming what you feel so you can work with it
Gentle reflection practices like gratitude, savoring, and values check-ins
detail.approach: Solace meets you where you are. It uses open-ended invitations — "What feels true for you right now?" — instead of directives. Responses are warm, spacious, and unhurried, like a calm conversation over tea. It normalizes the full range of human experience, including the messy parts.

list.name: Momentum
list.desc: Holds you accountable to your goals — and knows what actually derails you. Uses Motivational Interviewing and behavioral science to keep you moving forward without burning out. Action over theory.

detail.subtitle: Growth coach — direct, honest, action-oriented

theories.name: Motivational Interviewing (Miller & Rollnick)
theories.desc: Evokes your own motivation instead of imposing external pressure. Explores ambivalence without judgment — because pushing harder doesn't work when the resistance is internal.

theories.name: Implementation Intentions (Gollwitzer)
theories.desc: Bridges the gap between wanting and doing with "When [situation], I will [behavior]" — turning vague intentions into automatic responses.

theories.name: Behavioral Activation
theories.desc: When motivation is low, start with low-effort, high-value actions to build momentum. Movement creates motivation, not the other way around.

theories.name: SMART Goals
theories.desc: Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound — a framework that turns "I want to be better" into something you can actually track and achieve.

useCases: Setting and tracking goals with someone who remembers your commitments across sessions
Breaking through procrastination by identifying your specific triggers and energy cycles
Breaking large projects into progressive milestones with clear next actions
Getting honest feedback — not cheerleading — when you're avoiding something
Recalibrating priorities when what mattered last month no longer fits
detail.approach: Momentum is direct and clear — no fluff. It celebrates wins by connecting them to strategy and effort, not luck. It respects that rest and recovery are legitimate strategies, not failures. And it always leaves you with something concrete you can do.

transparency.title: You see everything it knows
transparency.description: The Memory Explorer shows your full knowledge graph. Inspect it, correct it, or delete from it. You're always in control.

features.title: Explore your graph
features.desc: Interactive visualization of every entity and relationship in your graph.

features.title: Correct in plain English
features.desc: "I left TechCorp." The graph updates. No forms, no menus.

features.title: Fully open source
features.desc: The entire codebase is public. See how it works, fork it, contribute.

features.title: Export to Notion
features.desc: Sync your graph to Notion. Review offline. Push corrections back.

pricing.title: Choose your depth of memory
